paper_title: Efficient Ensemble for Fine-tuning Language Models on Multiple Datasets
caption: We compare error rate (one minus accuracy), computation cost, and memory usage across our approach and baselines when fine-tuning Llama-3-8B on ten NLP tasks. MTL-FT refers to first fine-tuning a shared LoRA on all the datasets, and then fine-tuning the low-rank adapter on each dataset, while Full FT refers to full fine-tuning of the entire model. Our approach boosts the test accuracy of QLoRA by 10\% on average, only incurring 8\% additional computation and 9 GB more memory. It performs on par with the best baseline with 45\% less FLOPs.

model_annotations.Bulgarian: The bar chart, titled “QLoRA,” compares the computational cost, measured in FLOPs (floating-point operations), across six different fine-tuning methods for the Llama-3-8B model on ten NLP tasks, as described in the associated paper. The vertical axis, labeled “# FLOPs,” is displayed on a logarithmic scale ranging from 10¹⁸ to 10²⁰, with major gridlines at each power of ten. The horizontal axis lists six methods: “Full FT,” “TAG,” “LoRA,” “MTL-FT,” “QLoRA,” and “Ours,” arranged in descending order of FLOPs. The first five methods are represented by orange bars, while the “Ours” method is highlighted in green. “Full FT” has the highest computational cost, exceeding 10¹⁹ FLOPs, followed closely by “TAG” and “LoRA,” both slightly below 10¹⁹. “MTL-FT” and “QLoRA” show progressively lower costs, with “QLoRA” near 10¹⁸.5. The “Ours” method, while visually comparable in height to “QLoRA,” is explicitly noted in the caption to incur only 8% additional computation relative to QLoRA and to achieve 45% fewer FLOPs than the best baseline, suggesting it is computationally more efficient despite similar visual height on the logarithmic scale. No error bars or additional annotations are present on the bars themselves.
model_annotations.English: The bar chart, titled “QLoRA,” illustrates the computational cost, measured in FLOPs (floating-point operations), for six different fine-tuning methods applied to the Llama-3-8B model across ten NLP tasks, as described in the paper “Efficient Ensemble for Fine-tuning Language Models on Multiple Datasets.” The vertical axis, labeled “# FLOPs,” uses a logarithmic scale ranging from 10¹⁸ to 10²⁰, with major gridlines at each power of ten. The horizontal axis lists the six methods: “Full FT,” “TAG,” “LoRA,” “MTL-FT,” “QLoRA,” and “Ours,” each represented by a single vertical bar. The first five bars are colored orange, while the final bar, “Ours,” is distinctively colored green, visually emphasizing the proposed method. The bars are arranged in descending order of FLOP count: “Full FT” is the most computationally expensive, with a value slightly below 10²⁰; “TAG” and “LoRA” follow closely with values around 10¹⁹.⁵ and 10¹⁹.³ respectively; “MTL-FT” is next at approximately 10¹⁹.¹; “QLoRA” is lower at roughly 10¹⁸.⁷; and “Ours” is the least expensive, at approximately 10¹⁸.⁶. The chart visually supports the caption’s claim that the proposed method (“Ours”) achieves performance comparable to the best baseline while requiring significantly fewer FLOPs — specifically, 45% less than the best-performing baseline, which appears to be “QLoRA” based on the relative bar heights and the context provided.
model_annotations.German: Das Balkendiagramm mit dem Titel „QLoRA“ vergleicht die berechneten FLOPs (Floating Point Operations) verschiedener Fine-tuning-Methoden für das Sprachmodell Llama-3-8B auf zehn NLP-Aufgaben, wobei die vertikale Achse die Anzahl der FLOPs in logarithmischer Skala von 10¹⁸ bis 10²⁰ anzeigt und die horizontale Achse sechs Methoden in absteigender Reihenfolge ihrer FLOPs auflistet: „Full FT“, „TAG“, „LoRA“, „MTL-FT“, „QLoRA“ und „Ours“. Die ersten fünf Balken sind in Orange gehalten, während der letzte Balken, „Ours“, in Grün dargestellt ist, was ihn visuell hervorhebt. Der höchste Balken, „Full FT“, erreicht etwa 5 × 10¹⁹ FLOPs, gefolgt von „TAG“ mit etwa 4 × 10¹⁹, „LoRA“ mit etwa 3 × 10¹⁹, „MTL-FT“ mit etwa 1.5 × 10¹⁹, „QLoRA“ mit etwa 1 × 10¹⁹ und „Ours“ mit etwa 8 × 10¹⁸ FLOPs. Die Balken sind nicht gruppiert oder gestapelt, sondern stellen jeweils eine einzelne Methode dar, und ihre Höhe entspricht direkt dem logarithmischen Wert der FLOPs. Die Beschriftungen der Kategorien sind diagonal unter den Balken angeordnet, und die Skala der y-Achse ist logarithmisch mit Tick-Markierungen bei 10¹⁸, 10¹⁹ und 10²⁰. Der Balken „Ours“ ist der niedrigste und repräsentiert somit die Methode mit den geringsten berechneten FLOPs im Vergleich zu den anderen aufgeführten Ansätzen.
